name: Replit

modes.label: Reserved VM deployment (always-on shared/dedicated VM, hourly)
modes.commit_note: Reserved VMs are always-on deployments (docs: 'Guaranteed compute resources that run continuously'), so the mode is priced only for always-on instances; per-shift stop/start is undocumented; docs list monthly prices $15 / $35 / $50 / $130 (= hourly x ~720 h) for the first four sizes. 8 and 16 vCPU sizes only appear in the Aug-2026 hourly table (~$260 / ~$520 at 720 h, derived).
modes.note: Hourly rates from the Aug-2026 cloud billing update (effective first billing cycle on/after 2026-08-01). One Reserved VM = one published app; it runs continuously and is billed whether busy or idle. Whether it can be stopped between shifts to save money is not documented (always-on product). Paid from plan credits first, then pay-as-you-go. Disk per VM unpublished (plan storage per app 50 GiB Core / 256 GiB Pro). Verified 2026-09-28: 'Guaranteed compute resources that run continuously' at flat monthly prices per size (docs.replit.com/billing/deployment-pricing) = billed on allocation.

modes.label: Autoscale / Scheduled deployment (compute units while serving or running)
modes.note: $0.60 per 1M compute units; 1 CPU-second = 18 CU ($0.03888/vCPU-h), 1 GB-second RAM = 2 CU ($0.00432/GiB-h). Plus $0.40 per 1M requests and a per-deployment base fee ($2/mo on the deployment-pricing page; $1/mo in the Aug-2026 update table: conflict). Billed only while serving requests (concurrent requests share an instance); instance goes idle after 15 min without traffic. Request-driven web apps only, not interactive sandboxes (hence 'alt'). Machine size options and max machines are set in the UI but not published. Verified 2026-09-28: cost is 'a unit of cloud computing based on the CPU and memory you choose'; 'You pay while requests are being served. When your app is idle, it scales to zero and costs nothing to run' (docs.replit.com/features/publishing/machine-configuration.md); 'Pay only when your app serves requests - nothing when idle', instance 'goes idle after 15 minutes of inactivity' (deployment-pricing). So basis = chosen machine size (alloc) during request-serving time only (autoscale_busy_share knob); the 15-min warm tail is not described as billed. MERGED 2026-09-28 with the former 'scheduled' regime (Scheduled deployments: identical $0.60/1M CU rate, $2/mo base fee, cron batch runs; scheduler free).

plans.name: Starter (free)
plans.note: Daily Agent credits (capped monthly) + monthly credits for databases/storage/publishing (amounts unpublished). Only 1 published app, which expires after 30 days (concurrency 1 = one deployment). Publishes to North America only; no region choice. trial_only (verified 2026-09-28, docs.replit.com/billing/plans/starter-plan): 'One free published app' that 'will automatically go down after 30 days'; monthly credits cover 'Publishing (Autoscale, static)' only; additional published apps require Core or Pro. Can't host an always-on Reserved VM workload.

plans.name: Core
plans.note: $20/mo ($18/mo billed annually) includes $20 monthly credits covering Agent, deployments, databases, storage; credits reset monthly (no rollover). Overage pay-as-you-go up to a budget. 5 collaborators; 100 GiB dev + 100 GiB deployment outbound; 50 GiB storage per app; Free Mode agent chat up to 30 h.

plans.name: Pro $100
plans.note: $100/mo ($90 annual) with $100 credits; unused credits roll over for two months. Up to 15 builders (no per-user fee), 50 viewers, 10 parallel agents, 1,000 GiB dev outbound, 100 GiB deployment outbound, 256 GiB storage per app, 28-day DB rollback.

plans.name: Pro $250
plans.note: Pro credit tier ($215/mo billed annually). Credits assumed equal to the monthly tier amount (pricing page tier selector); rollover two months.

plans.name: Pro $2,500
plans.note: Pro credit tier ($2,000/mo billed annually, i.e. 20% off).

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.note: Self-serve upgrade from any plan (or via sales). Billing model chosen at checkout: 'Credit commitment - a fixed annual credit purchase' or 'Pay-as-you-go - charged via the billing method on file once you exceed your credit limit'. Commitment slider in the docs screenshot spans $10,000-$200,000/year (alt text). Unlimited seats, no per-seat costs; SSO/SAML + SCIM, audit logs via SIEM, per-user spend limits, geography enforcement, static outbound IPs. 'Single-tenant with VPC' is marked 'Coming soon' on the pricing page. Keep flags ['sales'] (annual commit).

plans.name: Core (annual)
plans.note: Billed annually ($216/yr up front), still $20 monthly credits, which reset monthly. 1-year commitment.

plans.name: Pro $2,500 (annual)
plans.note: Effective 20% discount on the first $2,500/mo of usage with a 1-year commitment.

perf_source: No benchmark row: provider is not in ComputeSDK results or the HPC run (as of 2026-09-28). See research/perf-map.json.

knobs.label: Share of session time an Autoscale instance is serving requests
knobs.why: Autoscale bills CPU/RAM only while requests are in flight (overlapping requests share the instance); idle gaps cost nothing.

caveats: Replit is an AI app builder / IDE + hosting platform, not a programmatic sandbox API. Reserved VM = one always-on published app; there is no API to spin up N ephemeral VMs.

Development workspace time is 'Unlimited' on Core/Pro and not billed per hour, but workspace vCPU/RAM per plan is no longer published (usage docs say 'determined by plan'). THIRD-PARTY ONLY: Core workspace 4 vCPU / 8 GiB, Starter 2 GiB RAM (nocode.mba / eesel.ai / p0stman.com). Hard limit: 20 concurrent Replit Apps per account. Not modelled as a mode.
Agent usage is effort-based (billed per checkpoint by task complexity, at provider API rates) and is deducted from the same credits; Core/Pro get a daily 'Free Mode' allowance. Not modelled.

Reserved VM hourly rates come from the Aug-2026 update table; the deployment-pricing page lists monthly prices ($15/$35/$50/$130) that equal ~720 h. Engine at 730 h gives ~1.4% more. Whether a Reserved VM can be stopped to avoid charges is undocumented, so reserved-vm has requires_always_on=true (verifier 2026-09-28; before, the engine billed it per session hour, the 'unverified' $1,589 scenario in the regime file, instead of the documented always-on $6,500).

Autoscale base fee conflict (re-confirmed 2026-09-28): deployment-pricing page constants AutoscaleBaseFee '$2' / AutoscaleDeployment '$2.00' vs the Aug-2026 update table 'Autoscale base fee $1 / mo' in both the current and new columns. Unresolved; base fee not modelled (start_fee 0). Autoscale machine sizes and max machines not published. Request fee $0.40/1M not modelled.

Pro tiers verified from the rendered pricing page 2026-09-29: $100 ($90/mo annual), $250 ($215), $500 ($425), $1,000 ($825), $2,500 ($2,000). The selector labels each tier by its credit amount ('$100 credits'), and the FAQ says 'Pro subscribers get at least $100 in monthly credits'.

Aug 2026 price cut (effective first billing cycle on/after 2026-08-01): CU $3.20 -> $0.60/1M, requests $1.20 -> $0.40/1M, outbound $0.10 -> $0.05/GiB, App Storage $0.03 -> $0.015/GiB-mo, DB storage $1.50 -> $0.35/GiB-mo; Reserved VMs changed per size (dedicated 4/16 $0.22 -> $0.1806/h; legacy shared 1/4 rose $0.042 -> $0.0486/h).
Outbound: 100 GiB/month included for deployments on Core and Pro (plus 100 GiB Core / 1,000 GiB Pro for development), then $0.05/GiB; ingress free. Egress free allowance encoded per account.

Storage: no snapshot/paused-state billing (snapshot_gib_month null). App Storage (object) $0.015/GiB-mo; production PostgreSQL $0.16/compute-hour (suspends after 5 min idle) + $0.35/GiB-mo, 10 GiB limit per DB.
Credit packs $100-$1,000 (up to $50 off), expire after 6 months; budgets are hard caps that suspend usage-based services.
Pro tier credits assumed equal to the monthly price of each tier (pricing page shows '$100 credits' on the tier selector; higher tiers' credit amounts not explicitly restated).
Regions: North America, Europe, Asia, South America, Australia selectable on Core/Pro/Enterprise (permanent per project); no regional price differences published.
No benchmark data (perf null). Isolation 'container' is unverified; published apps run on GCP.

Unverified (2026-09-28): Autoscale compute units are described both as 'CPU time: Processing power used' and as 'based on the CPU and memory you choose'; card keeps alloc (configured size x request-serving time). If Replit meters actual CPU seconds, a mostly-idle-while-serving app costs less on CPU.

SSH (verified 2026-09-28, docs.replit.com/replit-workspace/ssh): SSH connects to a Replit App's development workspace and is 'available for Core, Pro, and all other paid plans'; SSH into published deployments (Reserved VM / Autoscale) is not documented, so those regimes carry ssh = null. Card-level ssh = true refers to the (unmodelled) workspace.
App Storage objects have a 7-day minimum billing period; App Storage data transfer is $0.05/GiB (source: docs.replit.com/billing/object-storage-billing).
Credit packs (Core/Pro): $100 for $100, $300 for $290, $500 for $480, $1,000 for $950; they expire 6 months after purchase, used earliest-expiring first, with optional auto-reload.

fleet.tiers: Starter includes 1 free published app, expiring after 30 days with republish allowed. Core/Pro add usage credits and paid deployment options.
fleet.notes: Published-app allowance is not a concurrent-machine limit: Autoscale and Reserved VM have different models. No aggregate new-account VM/vCPU/GPU quota or verification/approval timeline found.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

harness_api.quote: Start an Agent update for an existing app.
harness_api.note: Replit MCP Server (https://mcp.replit.com/server/mcp, OAuth) drives Replit's own Agent from outside: create_app_from_prompt, update_app_using_prompt (follow-ups), ask_question, list_apps, publish_app, get_publish_status. Replit Agent only (no Claude Code/Codex inside); no documented event streaming or conversation resume; MCP rather than REST SDK.

ingress_rules.quote: **Invite only**: Only you, admins, invited groups, and invited users.
ingress_rules.note: Published apps: Public / Password protected / Workspace only / Invite only (Replit sign-in gate); external access tokens let services reach private deployments; private dev URLs; Enterprise admins can require private deployments. Reserved VM config includes port mappings. No IP allowlist documented.

secret_proxy.quote: When you use Replit AI Integrations, Replit manages the provider credentials and bills you at the public API price.
secret_proxy.note: Replit-managed LLM gateway (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Grok, OpenRouter) billed to credits; the user never holds a provider key. Other secrets are env vars via the Secrets pane; Connectors are OAuth integrations (token handling not described as a proxy). No non-HTTP coverage.

volume_attach.quote: Avoid saving and relying on data written to a published app's filesystem.
volume_attach.note: No attachable block/network volumes. Persistent data goes to App Storage (GCS-backed object storage via API, not mounted) or PostgreSQL. Workspace has up to 50-256 GiB storage per app by plan.

volume_shared.quote: Each bucket belongs to one project and cannot be shared across apps.
volume_shared.note: App Storage bucket is shared between dev and prod of the same app (and all Autoscale instances) but via object API, not a mounted filesystem; not shareable across apps.

image_oci.quote: Replit uses Nix to manage packages and environments. The replit.nix file is used for: Specifying system dependencies
image_oci.note: Environments are configured via .replit + replit.nix (Nix packages), not by supplying your own Docker/OCI image. Card-level custom_image is already false.

nested_virt.quote: Replit turns ideas, everyday work, and intelligence into useful outcomes
nested_virt.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Replit is an AI app-builder/IDE + hosting platform on Nix-managed workspaces/deployments; no /dev/kvm or nested-virtualization capability is documented anywhere in the docs.

browser.quote: VNC is a mature virtual desktop protocol that allows your Replit App to stream a native desktop to your web browser.
browser.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Replit provides a webview/preview pane to view your own app's output and an optional VNC desktop stream, not a managed real browser instance for general browsing/automation.

anti_bot.quote: Replit turns ideas, everyday work, and intelligence into useful outcomes
anti_bot.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. Replit is an app-builder/hosting platform, not a browser-automation product; no stealth/fingerprinting-evasion features are documented.

captcha_solving.quote: Replit turns ideas, everyday work, and intelligence into useful outcomes
captcha_solving.note: not offered: outside the product's scope. No CAPTCHA-solving capability documented; not relevant to an app-builder/hosting platform.

egress_ip_type.quote: Replit hosts data primarily in Google Cloud Platform (GCP) data centers in the United States, with an optional hosting region in India
egress_ip_type.note: Replit Apps/VMs run on GCP infrastructure; outbound IPs (including Enterprise's static outbound IPs) are ordinary GCP datacenter IPs, not residential/mobile.

snapshot_auto.quote: A checkpoint is a complete snapshot of your Replit App state created automatically by Agent at key development milestones.
snapshot_auto.note: Checkpoints (files, DB contents, environment config, Agent memory) are captured automatically without an explicit API/CLI call, and can be rolled back to restore that state.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: A checkpoint is a complete snapshot of your Replit App state created automatically by Agent at key development milestones.
snapshot_on_demand.note: Checkpoint creation is described only as automatic (Agent-driven, at milestones); no documented manual/API call to trigger a checkpoint or snapshot on demand.

fork_running.note: Fork (card-level fork=true) copies a Repl's files/environment into a new App; it is a code/environment clone, not a clone of a live running machine's in-memory process state, so cloning a running instance without stopping it is not documented.

pause_resume.quote: Reserved VM: Your server is always on, so you pay a fixed monthly cost for the chosen configuration.
pause_resume.note: Reserved VM deployments are documented as always-on with no pause option; Autoscale instead scales to zero/wakes on request (a different mechanism, see wake_on_request), and no explicit pause/resume (with paused or reduced billing) API is documented for either.

wake_on_request.quote: App starts up when the first request arrives (if idle). Processes the request using compute resources. Goes idle after 15 minutes of inactivity.
wake_on_request.note: Autoscale Deployments scale to zero when idle and automatically start on the next incoming request.

live_resize.quote: Apply your changes: Publish your app again after changing the configuration. The new machine settings take effect with the new deployment.
live_resize.note: Changing CPU/RAM (machine configuration) requires republishing/redeploying the app; it is not a live resize of a running machine.

own_agent_api.quote: Start an Agent update for an existing app.
own_agent_api.note: Replit's own agent is a coding/app-building agent (already covered by harness_api via the MCP server: create_app_from_prompt, update_app_using_prompt, ask_question). Replit does not offer a separate first-party browser/computer-use/research task-agent API distinct from that coding agent.

egress_allowlist.quote: Use Privacy settings to control published-app access and protect development URLs.
egress_allowlist.note: Enterprise privacy/deployment controls (private deployments, password protection, geography enforcement) govern inbound access and publish geography, not provider-side outbound allow/deny lists or no-internet modes. No egress allowlist feature documented.

egress_http_rules.quote: Use Privacy settings to control published-app access and protect development URLs.
egress_http_rules.note: No documented provider-side egress rules at HTTP method/path granularity; documented controls are for inbound access privacy, not outbound traffic shaping.

soc2.quote: Replit has achieved SOC 2 Type 2 Attestation of Compliance, demonstrating our ongoing commitment to security best practices and controls.
soc2.note: Also stated on trust.replit.com: 'Replit is SOC 2 Type II audited annually by an independent CPA firm.'

hipaa.quote: GCP is an industry-leading cloud provider, certified for compliance with ISO 27001 and SOC 2 Type 2. Additionally, Replit has achieved SOC 2 Type 2 Attestation of Compliance
hipaa.note: Replit's security/compliance overview and trust center list SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 (via GCP) but do not mention HIPAA eligibility or BAA availability anywhere in the docs or trust center.

max_session_h.quote: Reserved VM Deployments: Guaranteed compute resources that run continuously.
max_session_h.note: Reserved VM is documented as running continuously with no maximum session duration; it runs until explicitly stopped/undeployed (whether it can be paused mid-run to save cost is itself undocumented, per the card's commit_note).

memory_snapshot_fork.quote: Agent also creates checkpoints as it works, so you can roll back to any previous state.
memory_snapshot_fork.note: Replit's fork/checkpoint mechanism copies project files (code, and 'fork' duplicates a Repl into a new project) and Agent checkpoints are code/DB rollback points, not a live memory/process snapshot; no docs describe forking a running app with its in-memory process state intact.

docker_inside.quote: Replit uses `Nix` to manage packages and environments.
docker_inside.note: Replit Apps are configured via .replit/replit.nix and system dependencies are managed through the Nix package manager, not Docker; Replit historically ran on Docker internally (REPL_IMAGE env var exposes the underlying image) but publicly moved app environments to Nix, and no docs describe running/managing Docker containers inside a Replit workspace or deployment.

computer_use.quote: VNC is a mature virtual desktop protocol that allows your Replit App to stream a native desktop to your web browser.
computer_use.note: The desktop feature is a human-facing VNC stream for viewing/interacting with native GUI apps in-browser; there is no documented programmatic API to drive the desktop via screenshots+clicks (computer-use API).

custom_image.quote: Replit uses `Nix` to manage packages and environments.
custom_image.note: Environments are built by declaring Nix packages in replit.nix / .replit, not by supplying a custom Docker/OCI base image; no docs describe bringing your own container image for a workspace or deployment.

volumes.quote: Avoid saving and relying on data written to a published app's filesystem.
volumes.note: No attachable block/network volume product exists; persistent data goes through App Storage (GCS-backed object storage via API, not a mounted volume) or PostgreSQL. Matches the card's own volume_attach/volume_shared=false evidence.

public_ipv4.note: Pricing page only advertises 'Static outbound IPs' (egress, Enterprise) and inbound access is via replit.dev/replit.app HTTPS domains behind Replit's proxy; no product offers a public IPv4 address assigned to a machine.

gpu.quote: Guaranteed compute resources that run continuously
gpu.note: Reserved VM sizes are CPU/RAM only (0.5-16 vCPU, 2-64 GiB); no GPU SKU, GPU pricing row, or GPU mention exists anywhere in docs.replit.com llms-full.txt or the pricing page.

windows.note: 'Windows' only appears as an OS for the Replit Desktop client app (the IDE UI) and in generic OS-shortcut text (Ctrl vs Cmd); the actual workspace/deployment compute runs Linux containers only (Reserved VM os: linux). No Windows guest/VM product exists.

macos.quote: The Replit Desktop App is a redesigned, native app for Windows and Mac.
macos.note: Same as windows: macOS is only the OS the Replit Desktop *client* runs on, not a macOS guest machine you can rent; deployments/workspaces are Linux-only.

arm64.note: doubtful "no" could not be confirmed: No architecture (x86_64/arm64) is mentioned anywhere in the deployment-pricing docs, machine-configuration docs, or llms-full.txt dump; Replit does not publish CPU architecture for its VMs. Kept as false/unclear since there's no first-party statement of ARM availability either way.

self_host.quote: All published apps are hosted in the United States. Enterprise customers can contact sales to request their published apps to be hosted in the European Union instead.
self_host.note: Even region choice for Enterprise is limited to Replit-run regions (US/EU); there is no on-prem / self-hosted Replit product documented anywhere.

byoc.note: Enterprise 'Single-tenant with VPC' is explicitly marked 'Coming soon' on the pricing page, i.e. not currently available, and even that describes an isolated tenant on Replit's own infra (GCP), not deployment into the customer's own cloud account (BYOC).

open_source.quote: Replit's infrastructure is backed by Google Cloud Platform (GCP).
open_source.note: Replit is a closed-source commercial SaaS platform; only incidental third-party open-source components are referenced in docs (e.g. Eruda dev tools, the community Skills repo), not the core Replit product/platform itself.

cpu_class.quote: Dedicated compute resources with predictable monthly costs. #### Shared VMs | 0.5 vCPU / 2GB RAM | ... #### Dedicated VMs | 1 vCPU / 4GB RAM | ... | 2 vCPU / 8GB RAM | ... | 4 vCPU / 16GB RAM |
cpu_class.note: Reserved VM explicitly separates a legacy 'Shared VMs' tier (0.5 vCPU/2GB, shared vCPU) from 'Dedicated VMs' tiers (1, 2, 4, 8, 16 vCPU, dedicated/reserved cores) — the pricing page literally headers them 'Shared VMs' vs 'Dedicated VMs' and the accordion summary says 'Choose shared or dedicated VMs based on your performance needs.' Five of the six published sizes are dedicated; only the smallest (0.5 vCPU) is shared, so the mode-level value here reflects the dedicated majority (matches the card's `sizes[].name` fields, which already label each size 'shared' or 'dedicated'). Autoscale's CPU class (shared vs dedicated vCPU while serving requests) is not stated anywhere in the docs, so it is omitted per field instructions (only include modes with evidence).
